subject.title: fix(browser): bound client fetch success JSON reads

question: Should browser-control HTTP success responses be capped at 32 MiB, accepting that larger successful external browser-control JSON responses now fail instead of resolving?
rationale: The patch is the right owner-boundary fix for the buffering bug, but it intentionally fail-closes an existing success path for oversized responses and the limit is a product/compatibility contract.

options.title: Accept the 32 MiB cap
options.body: Merge with the new browser-control success-response size boundary because it preserves the documented large `response/body` envelope while preventing unbounded buffering.

options.title: Tune the cap before merge
options.body: Ask for a different browser-specific limit or a named shared helper if maintainers know supported browser-control responses may exceed 32 MiB.

options.title: Pause for contract confirmation
options.body: Keep the PR open until browser-control response-size expectations are explicit enough to accept the fail-closed behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept the 32 MiB cap
recommendation.body: Merge with the new browser-control success-response size boundary because it preserves the documented large `response/body` envelope while preventing unbounded buffering.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is assigned on the PR and authored the current-head cap adjustment from 16 MiB to 32 MiB.
